A Global has no Draft: saving it publishes it, on every forge.

On github, a save is a commit, as it is for a page. The Globals section then shows the same building… and live status as an Editor variant, because a static site's readers see the change only once the site rebuilds.
On the local forge, the save writes the file in your checkout.
On the server forge, the save writes and publishes in one action.

A Global's fields are validated before the save, down to each item of a nested list. An error names its field and shows beside the offending item, so an editor can fix a missing link label in the third footer column without hunting for it. If someone else saved the Global after the form was opened, the save is refused and the conflict banner appears, as it does for a page. It offers to download the editor's version, reload the latest, or dismiss, and nothing is overwritten silently.
